newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - Aug 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - Aug 18.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- The South Korean government plans to speed up investigation into spies for North Korea, particularly those mentioned by top North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop, following last week's defection to the North by Oh Ik-jae, 68, a former South Korean religious leader.

- A ship carrying journalists and representatives of the United States, South Korea, Japan and the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organiastion (KEDO) will leave for North Korea today. They will attend a ground-breaking ceremony for the construction of nuclear power plants in the communist country.
- Kia Group Chairman Kim Sun-hong denied that he discussed the possibility of his resignation with senior government and ruling party officials to help rescue the troubled conglomerate.

- The government last Saturday welcomed a Japanese court's dismissal of criminal charges brought against the skipper of a South Korean fishing boat for entering the newly claimed Japanese territorial waters.
